result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\.

My overall pick is **1Password for ease of use and team collaboration**, while Bitwarden is the better choice if keeping costs down is important.

Here are the options I'd shortlist in November 2026.

## Best password managers for small teams

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password Business** (Best overall experience)

# \$8.99

USD per user/month, annual billing

- Excellent shared vaults and permissions
- Easy onboarding for non-technical staff
- Admin controls and security reporting
- Good integrations with business tools

[1Password business plans](https://1password.com/business)

- Excellent value

- Audit logs and directory synchronisation

**3\. Keeper Business**

Privacy-focused alternative

- Strong privacy focus
- End-to-end encrypted vaults
- Secure sharing
- Useful email alias functionality

[Proton Pass business plans](https://proton.me/business/pass)

Pricing is indicative, in USD, generally billed annually. Check Australian pricing, GST and plan limits before purchasing. Sources: [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[cybercred.com.au](https://cybercred.com.au/articles/password-managers-compared-for-small-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[velotouch.com](https://velotouch.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommendation

| Your priority | My choice |
|--------|--------|
| Best overall usability | 1Password |
| Best value for money | Bitwarden |
| More advanced administration | Keeper |
| Privacy-focused approach | Proton Pass |


For a typical small business, I'd lean towards 1Password. The extra cost can be worthwhile if it makes the system easier for everyone to adopt and use correctly.

## Three things I'd insist on

Whichever product you choose, make sure it has\:

1. **Shared team vaults** – staff can share company credentials without sending passwords through email or Slack.
2. **Access management** – you can revoke someone's access immediately when they leave.
3. **Two-factor authentication** – protect the password manager itself with an additional authentication method.

## A couple of questions to narrow it down

I can make a more specific recommendation if I know\:

**1\. How many people are on your team?**

---

**3\. What does your business primarily use?**
